title: Freshness check silently skips records whose recorded range is a single commit

finding.claim: Freshness check silently skips records whose recorded range is a single commit
finding.evidence: When a record has a truthy 'range', the code always calls git rev-list on it and only falls back to 'head' when that returns None. For a single-commit range, rev-list returns an empty set rather than None, so the later 'head' fallback is skipped and the record is treated as not touching any span.
finding.recommendation: Treat an empty commit set from '_commit_set' as unresolved for this purpose, or explicitly detect single-commit ranges and include the recorded head/commit itself before deciding whether the record touches the span.

refutation.reason: The quoted line shows the code calls _commit_set with the range string, but the finding's claim that rev-list returns an empty set for single-commit ranges and skips the head fallback is not supported by the visible code. The region does not contain the _commit_set implementation or the subsequent h

probe.summary: Disputes probe (`probes/closing_disputes_probe.py`, section c): synthetic records were placed against a span containing their head. A record with the degenerate range `X..X` (rev-list yields an EMPTY set — not None, so the head fallback never ran) appeared in NEITHER the touching nor the unscoped list: silently dropped from the freshness check, although its head is inside the span. (A bare-sha range behaves oppositely — rev-list returns the commit and its ancestors.) FIXED in this workup: an empty resolution now falls back to the recorded head, and a record with neither lands in unscoped — named, never silent. Parent-fail verified by two new tests.
